Mary Kemph

What every machine in your gym does

Setting up

There are three main adjustments to make, and they carry for pretty much any machine in the gym.

  • The seat. Look for a yellow handle or a pin under it. Sit in the machine first, then set the height — the part of you that is doing the moving should line up with the round pivot on the side.
  • The pad or the roller. Same handle, same idea. It should already be touching you before you start. A gap means it hits you when you move.
  • The pin in the stack. The weight is a stack of plates with a pin in the side. Pull it out, push it into the hole beside the number you want. Start lighter than you think.

Every machine has a diagram on it showing the movement. It's not perfect, but it's a good start.

01Legs and hips

Leg pressPUSH

Butt and quads

You sit back into it and push the footplate away with both feet.

Seat back far enough that your knees start bent, not squashed into your chest.

Leg extensionPUSH

Quads

A roller sits across your shins and you straighten your knees against it.

Roller just above your ankle. The back of your knee touching the seat edge.

Leg curlPULL

Hamstrings

Almost the same seat, opposite job. You bend your knees and drag the roller under you.

Roller behind your ankles, thigh pad down snug so your legs cannot lift.

Multi hipBOTH

Butt and hips

Handy, but we don't often use this. You stand on one leg and move the other against a pad — forward, back, or out to the side.

Stand on the platform, hold the handles, set the pad to meet your thigh above the knee.

02Chest

Chest pressPUSH

Chest, shoulders, triceps

Back on the pad, and you push the two handles away from your chest.

Seat height so the handles sit level with the middle of your chest, not your throat.

Chest flyPUSH

Chest

Elbows on the two pads, and you squeeze your arms together in front of you. This is a variation of a Pec Fly machine as you'll see in Forge.

Seat so your elbows sit level with your shoulders. Both arms on the same setting.

03Back and arms

Lat PulldownPULL

Lats and traps

You sit under the wide bar, legs under the pads, and pull it down to your chest.

Thigh pads down firm enough that you do not lift off the seat when you pull.

The second pulldownPULL

Lats and traps

Same job as the lat pulldown. A belt across your lap instead of pads over your legs.

Belt across your hips, not your stomach, and pulled snug before you start.

Chest Supported RowPULL

Upper back and rear shoulder

Chest against the pad, and you draw the two arms back behind you.

Seat so the handles are at shoulder height and your chest reaches the pad without leaning.

Bicep curlPULL

Biceps

Arms laid flat on the sloped pad, and you bend your elbows. We do not often use this one, but you are welcome to substitute it in if it feels good.

Seat so your armpits rest on the top edge of the pad.

04Middle

Abdominal machinePULL

Abs

You hold the handles above your shoulders and curl forward against the pad.

Seat so the chest pad sits across your breastbone, feet hooked under the bar.

05The other room

Cable machineBOTH

Anything

Two cables you can set at any height, with a bar over the top for hanging.

The pulleys slide up and down the posts. Pull the pin, slide, push the pin back.

Chest press, the older oneBOTH

Chest, shoulders, triceps

The chrome frame in the far room. Same job as the chest press on the main floor.

Older kit, so the pins are stiffer. Same idea as everything else.

06Everything else

  • Treadmills, cross trainers and bikes along the windows.
  • A full rack of dumbbells, small plates, mats and balls.
  • Several benches that tip from flat to upright.
  • Two rowing machines in the far room, on rails under the window.
  • A pool through the window beside the leg press, and a room below the walkway set aside for floor work.
